blocks.x: Superintendent's Report
Halal-Certified School Meals & WRVC Recruiting Video
Discussion Summary

School Nutrition Director Mary Emerson reported that Westbrook is among the only U.S. school districts offering halal-certified meals districtwide. Emerson also reported that Westbrook High School was the first school in the nation to achieve certified K-12 halal service. The program is certified by the Islamic Food and Nutrition Council of America.

It was built with a regional Halal Meals Network (Portland, South Portland, and the Cumberland County Food Security Council). It launched at the high school in 2024. It expanded to the middle school last spring. It reached all three elementary schools this month.

For Ramadan (Feb. 17–Mar. 19, 2026) the high school will offer take-home meals via an after-hours vending machine. Emerson said the program has drawn interest from districts in Washington State, Vermont, and New York.

Director Gloria Noyes presented a new recruiting video for the Westbrook Regional Vocational Center (WRVC). It is unscripted and made of student testimonials. It covers early childhood education, electrical, automotive, emergency medical services and firefighting, culinary, and business programs.
Recruiting season is underway. Online applications open February 1.

Superintendent Dr. Peter Lancia separately corrected a date in the packet's FY27 budget calendar. The City Council's second budget reading will be May 4, 2026 at 6:00 PM, not April 4 as earlier circulated.
Key Decisions
No vote was taken. These were presentations.

Chair / Student / Committee Reports
Subcommittee Assignments, Annual Workshop & Student Report
Discussion Summary
Chair Andrea Mancuso announced subcommittee assignments for the year:
Finance: Noreen Poitras, Chair; Erin Cavallaro; Allison Brunette.
Facilities: Brooke Reed, Chair; Katy Rice.
Educational Programs: Katy Rice, Chair; Dr. Flynn Ross.
Policy: Erin Cavallaro, Chair; Andrea Mancuso.
The committee's annual orientation workshop with legal counsel is set for January 28 at 6:30 PM.

Mancuso also reported a recent joint meeting with the Mayor and city department heads. They reviewed the school department's capital improvement project submissions. She described it as productive ahead of a forthcoming conversation on shared municipal-school resource funding.

Student Representatives Jamila Mohamed Ahmed and Tina Nguyen reported that the high school's Bottles and Cans Club raised $3,600 before winter break. The money paid for $60 Hannaford gift cards for 60 Westbrook families facing food insecurity. They also gave updates from all three elementary schools (Saccarappa, Congin, Canal). The updates covered testing, events, and Canal's newly unveiled mascot, Cosmo Coyote.
Key Decisions
No vote was taken. These were reports.
Action Items
None.
Finance, Policy, Cell Phone Ad Hoc & Educational Programs Updates
Discussion Summary

The Finance Committee's January meeting was storm-cancelled and rescheduled to January 21. Chair Poitras reminded newer members that budget-review sessions require four members present. Facilities did not meet in December.

The Policy Committee (reported by Mancuso) found the district's homework policy outdated. It asked the leadership team to revise it. It tabled (set aside to take up later) a records-retention policy update pending a staff review.
The Policy Committee is also preparing a recommendation on Policy KEB (complaints against school personnel). The recommendation largely adopts Maine School Management Association model language.

The cell-phone ad hoc (temporary) committee (Cavallaro) surveyed high school students, faculty, and staff in December on cell phone use. This gathered baseline data ahead of vendor outreach and planned community forums this winter and spring.
Educational Programs (Rice) previewed three items.
First, the district is assuming new pre-K programming, likely at Canal School, as the state's Child Development Services program ends.
Second, an early-stage “intervention programming” framework aims at more tier-one classroom support.

Third, curriculum changes. They include a phased return from integrated “SM1/SM2” math to a traditional Algebra 1/Algebra 2/Geometry sequence. They also include a new Career and Technical Education Exploratory Program for sophomores. They also include a new Cooperative Education credit program, and continued growth in WRVC's cybersecurity program.
Key Decisions
No vote was taken. These were reports.

New Business
12.1 & 12.2 — Executive Session (Personnel Matter) & Same-Night Agreement Authorization
Discussion Summary

The committee recessed into executive session. This is a closed, private session allowed by state law for certain topics. It was held under 1 Maine Revised Statutes Annotated § 405(6)(A) to discuss a personnel matter.

Human Resources Director Martha Sumner and Assistant Superintendent of Operations and Finance Dr. Brian Mazjanis joined. The content of executive-session discussion is confidential by law and is not reflected in the source video or this summary.

Upon returning to open session, the committee amended the agenda to add item 12.2. The item authorizes the Superintendent to sign an agreement reached in that discussion and carry out its terms. It was taken up immediately as a combined first-and-final reading, meaning one vote that is both the first and the final, binding vote.
Key Decisions
Entered executive session: approved 7–0, moved by Chair Andrea Mancuso, seconded by Noreen Poitras.
Agenda amendment to add 12.2: approved 7–0, moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Erin Cavallaro.
Item 12.2 (agreement authorization, first and final reading): approved 7–0, moved by Katy Rice, seconded by Erin Cavallaro.

None.
Minutes Approval & Floor Correction (Dec. 10 & Dec. 18, 2025)
Discussion Summary

Chair Mancuso noted the December 18, 2025 minutes needed a floor amendment. The amendment would correctly reflect two things. After the recess that night, the committee voted 7–0 to enter executive session. And the committee adjourned directly from executive session without returning to open session.
Key Decisions

Minutes approved as amended, 6–0 with one abstention (Dr. Flynn Ross, per the approved minutes). Moved by Erin Cavallaro, seconded by Noreen Poitras. For: Andrea Mancuso, Katy Rice, Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Brooke Reed. Against: none.
